Bond markets brace for a long pause as inflation cools

Traders now expect the central bank to hold rates through the winter, and the yield curve has flattened to its narrowest gap in two years.

The central bank kept its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday for the tenth straight meeting, as retail inflation eased to 3.9% in August, the lowest reading since the pandemic.

Yields on the benchmark 10-year government bond fell three basis points to 6.42%, while two-year yields were little changed, flattening the curve between the two maturities.

"The market has largely priced in a long pause," said one fixed-income strategist, who added that a cut before March would need a sharper fall in food prices.

The bank also left the cash reserve ratio, the share of deposits lenders must park with it, unchanged at 4%, and kept its growth forecast for the year at 6.8%.
